citations.narrative:
Multiple rabbit enclosures have sections of the framing that are rusted to the point of significant flaking and pitting.
Multiple rabbit enclosures have sharp metal wire points present. Presence of flaking rust or sharp metal points in
enclosures could lead to injury of the animals housed within. Primary enclosures shall be structurally sound and
maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury.
Correct by 15 July 2026.

Floor space for an enclosure housing 3 weaned rabbits weighing approximately 2-3 pounds each is insufficient. The
enclosure measures 28 inches long by 21 inches wide and provides 4.1 square feet of space. The minimum floor space
for 3 weaned rabbits weighing less than 4.4 pounds is 4.5 square feet. Failure to provide sufficient space for rabbits may
result in their poor health or incompatibility. Each rabbit housed in a primary enclosure shall be provided a minimum
amount of floor space, exclusive of the space taken up by food and water receptacles, in accordance with the table in this
subpart.
Correct from this date forward of 15 June 2026.

A wooden block provided for chewing in a rabbit enclosure is covered in hair and excreta. More than half the wood is
saturated with white and brown material. A mound of fecal pellets is adhered to one end. Failure to adequately clean
enclosures may negatively affect the health of the animal. Primary enclosures shall be kept reasonably free of excreta,
hair, cobwebs and other debris by periodic cleaning.
Corrected at time of inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
